subject: Egress FQDN/SNI exception & proposed mTLS proxy for private endpoint
messages:
From: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress: allowlist feasibility and SNI/FQDN exceptions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the onboarding call this morning. One outstanding blocker from our networking team: we cannot commit to a static IP-based allowlist for the private endpoint. Our infra is set up to allow egress by FQDN/SNI only (company policy + ephemeral NATs).

Can Redwood provide an option that achieves the following?
- Allowlist by FQDN/SNI (we will not publish static IP blocks)
- Require mutually authenticated TLS from our proxy (client cert pinning)
- Preserve per-tenant egress logging (we need evidence for audit)

If you cannot support FQDN-only allowlisting, we need a short formal exception workflow and an evidence package for why IP-based allowlisting is required.

Regards,
Jun Sato
Network Security Engineer
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme-network-policy-summary.pdf (referenced)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jun Sato <jun.sato@octant.io>, Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist feasibility and SNI/FQDN exceptions

Jun — thanks for the clear context and the policy note. Replying with options so Acme security can pick the least disruptive path: 

Option A — FQDN/SNI + mTLS proxy (recommended) - We can front the private runtime with an egress proxy that accepts outbound connections from the customer proxy via mutual TLS. The Redwood ingress will validate the client cert (CA we agree on) and then forward to third-party hosts. Acme can continue to allow outbound egress by FQDN/SNI on your edge. Key properties:
  * Client authentication by mTLS; we pin Acme CA for the session.
  * SNI inspection at our proxy to route requests to the correct tenant/KV cache.
  * Per-request telemetry and tenant-level logs exported to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket (we can provide signed delivery).
  * No requirement for Acme to publish static IPs.

Option B — Static egress NATs with short rotation (if your policy mandates IP allowlist)
  * We can publish a small set of static NAT IP ranges. If your security policy forbids permanent static IPs, we can do scheduled rotations with a 72h window and provide attestations + rotation schedule and pre-notification.
  * This option increases audit overhead and requires an exception/risk assessment on your side.

Option C — Hybrid: FQDN allowlist for hosts we proxy to + a lightweight ACL for a small set of outbound TLS termination IPs used only for initial handshake to our proxy.

Questions/notes:
- For Option A we need Acme to provide the client cert CA bundle and the set of FQDNs you expect to access (wildcards accepted; we'll do SNI verification).
- We will not accept SNI-only without mTLS for production private endpoints (cannot authenticate tenant origin).
- We will sign an evidence bundle for audit: TLS session logs, SNI records, and delivery receipts.

Attaching a short diagram and an exportable CSV stub of what our safelist evidence looks like.

Next steps: please confirm which option you want by EOD Monday (2027-08-23). If Option A, share the CA bundle and one sample outbound FQDN list.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-mtls-proxy-diagram.pdf, safelist-evidence.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-21 13:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist feasibility and SNI/FQDN exceptions

Looping in Ben for NAT/IP operations and David for compliance notes. Two internal asks: 

1) Ben — can you prepare a short ops note (IP ranges, rotation cadence, how we sign attestations) in case Acme prefers Option B? We should include the change-window process and contact list.
2) David — if Acme selects Option A, we'll need to confirm the audit export format (JSONL vs CSV), retention period (default 90 days unless customer requests longer), and whether we can deliver logs to a customer-controlled bucket.

Also flagging that some customers expect wildcard FQDNs (e.g., *.example.com). We should document whether we do exact-match SNI or wildcard acceptance.

-Marissa
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist feasibility and SNI/FQDN exceptions

Naomi — thanks for the thoughtful options. Acme prefers Option A (FQDN/SNI + mTLS proxy). A few clarifying items before we sign off: 

1) Certificate lifecycle — we rotate client certs quarterly. Will Redwood accept a CA bundle that issues short-lived client certs? We need confirmation of compatible cert validity windows.
2) Wildcard FQDNs — we need to support wildcard entries for our SaaS partners (e.g., *.payments.acme.com). Please state whether Redwood will match wildcards on SNI.
3) Audit evidence — we require:
   - TLS session start/stop timestamps with SHA256 of client cert presented
   - SNI value per session and the resolved upstream FQDN
   - Delivery confirmation to customer bucket (signed manifest)

Can you provide a simple acceptance checklist and a PoC timeline? Our security approval board meets 2027-08-30.

Thanks,
Jun

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jun Sato <jun.sato@octant.io>, Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist feasibility and SNI/FQDN exceptions

Jun / Acme team — great, Option A is workable. Short answers and next steps below so you have a checklist for your security board: 

Certificate lifecycle
- We will accept CA bundles that issue short-lived certs. Our proxy validates the cert chain and enforces client cert revocation via CRL/OCSP. Recommended minimum lifetime: 72 hours; recommended maximum per our ops: 90 days. We will support quarterly rotation as you described.

Wildcard FQDNs
- We support wildcard SNI matches for entries of the form *.example.com. We do exact SNI match logic plus wildcard prefix matching — no regex matching.

Audit evidence (deliverables)
- TLS session log (jsonl) with timestamp, connection-id, client_cert_sha256, sni, upstream_fqdn, bytes_sent/recv.
- Signed delivery manifest to your S3/GCS (manifest contains object names + checksums).
- Rotation attestations for our NAT IPs (only if Option B used).

PoC and acceptance checklist (high level)
- 2027-08-23: Acme provides CA bundle and a representative FQDN list (<= 20 items).
- 2027-08-25: Redwood deploys PoC proxy in staging; provide test endpoints and logs.
- 2027-08-27: Joint runbook test (mutual TLS handshake, SNI routing, log delivery).
- 2027-08-30: Acme security board review & signoff.

Operational notes
- Log retention default: 90 days. Can be extended per contract.
- We will provide a signed SLA addendum for log delivery for enterprise contracted customers.
- For any future need to route by IP we will surface a formal exception form with risk summary.

I will circulate a short acceptance checklist (one page) and Ben will attach the ops note for Option B if needed.

Thanks — Naomi

Attachments: egress-mtls-proxy-diagram.pdf (diagram includes flow: Customer Proxy -> Redwood mTLS edge -> egress pool -> upstream hosts), safelist-evidence.csv (example)
